title: Count Beautiful Numbers
summary: Given two positive integers l and r, count the numbers between l and r (inclusive) whose digit product is divisible by their digit sum.
statement: Given two positive integers l and r, count the numbers between l and r (inclusive) whose digit product is divisible by their digit sum.
constraints: A positive integer is beautiful when its digit product is divisible by its digit sum.
Count beautiful integers in the inclusive range.
hints: The digit sum is at most nine times the digit count, so enumerate its final target value.
For each target sum, run a bounded digit DP tracking current sum, product remainder, whether a number started, and tightness.
Append each possible digit, multiplying the remainder after the first nonzero digit; accept exact target sum with remainder zero.
Every positive number belongs to exactly one target-sum DP, so summing targets counts each beautiful number once.
editorial: Every positive number belongs to exactly one target-sum DP, so summing targets counts each beautiful number once.

tests.explanation: Only two integers in this range satisfy product divisible by sum.
Every one-digit positive number has equal digit product and sum, so all nine qualify.
